input.quote: (a) This Agreement is governed in all respects by the laws of the State of Delaware without giving effect to its conflict of laws principles. Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York, New York.
input.rationale: Section 14(a) selects Delaware law (fallback-only under the playbook) while conferring exclusive jurisdiction on New York courts — an internally mismatched pairing. Since venue is already New York, the minimal edit to reach the preferred position is to change the governing law to New York. Venue is compliant (state and federal courts in New York, New York), and the arbitration in Section 8 is AAA-administered (not seated abroad), so no walk-away trigger; however Section 8's mandatory arbitration conflicts with the exclusive court jurisdiction and is flagged in the comment for conforming.

ops.oldText: the laws of the State of Delaware
ops.newText: the laws of the State of New York

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed the governing law from Delaware to New York so that it aligns with the exclusive New York venue already agreed in the same sentence; our playbook position is New York law with the state and federal courts in New York County. Please also note that the mandatory AAA arbitration in Section 8 is inconsistent with this exclusive court jurisdiction, and we would ask that Section 8 be conformed so disputes proceed in the New York courts.
proposal.summary: Change governing law from Delaware to New York to match the agreed New York exclusive venue.
